Veterans Day was initially known as Armistice Day, commemorating the end of World War I in 1918. In 1954, the holiday was renamed Veterans Day to honor all military veterans.

Veterans Day is about nationally commemorating and appreciating those who served in the armed forces, past and present. Across the U.S., the day is marked with parades, wreath-laying ceremonies, and moments of silence. Veterans Day also highlights qualities such as sacrifice, loyalty, and commitment to the greater good.

This past Monday, November the 11th, schools and departments across the school division took time to pause and reflect on the important work carried out by our military service members. For example, Principal Underwood and Ivy Elementary School honored and thanked over 120 veterans of students and staff members, families, and friends who served our country.

We are thankful for our active duty and retired military service members and appreciate the sacrifices they have made to protect us.

And whereas November 11, 2024 marks the 86th anniversary of Veterans Day being recognized as a national holiday,

on this day and every day we remember the millions of patriots who served and sacrificed for the betterment of our nation.
